corrections.why: LighthouseFriends records the light placed in operation on 17 September 1849, and the archive gives 1849 as the year established. The 1848 date is the directory's 'station established' and LighthouseFriends' year for the Pleasonton request.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The directory gives 1848 (station established); LighthouseFriends dates Pleasonton's request to 1848 and the lighting to 17 September 1849, which the archive also follows. The story uses 1849 and gives the directory's date.

notes_for_editor: Method: NRHP form (Massachusetts Lighthouse Information Form 41, NRIS 87001503), US Lighthouse Society archive place and roster, LighthouseFriends (facts only; paraphrased; its Lawrence log, 1878, 1890, 1908 and 1916 material is second-hand and not in the local corpus), Commissioner of Lighthouses reports for the fiscal years ended 30 June 1917, 1918, 1920 and 1922 (Internet Archive volume bub_gb_B2dYAAAAYAAJ, scan pages), Light-House Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1899 (scan page 90), Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1931 (PDF pp. 26, 30) and 1938 (PDF pp. 39-40), Rowlett's directory, and the 1881 Instructions for general context. Open conflicts, left for the reader: (1) first light 1848 (directory) against 1849 (LighthouseFriends, archive); (2) original optic fourth order and 1856 (LighthouseFriends) against fifth order (archive); (3) tower shape octagonal (NRHP) against hexagonal (archive, LighthouseFriends, directory); (4) the dwelling moved from Ned's Point dated to the 1870s (NRHP) and to 1888 (directory); (5) focal height 50 ft above mean high water (archive) against 38 ft above the ground in 1849 (LighthouseFriends); (6) deactivation 1945 (directory, archive) against LighthouseFriends' account of the light running several years after the 1947 sale. Checked against the page images: the 1931 Bulletin (PDF p. 26) reads 'June 18', so LighthouseFriends' 19 June is its own date; the 1938 Wings Neck paragraph (PDF p. 40) is in the hurricane article that begins on PDF p. 39, which gives 21 September; the 1917 volume (scan p. 257) and the 1920 and 1922 volumes (scan pp. 542, 742) are checked against their fiscal-year headings. The 1863 entry is known only through LighthouseFriends' summary (the Board's 1863 report is not in the local corpus). The 1849 Board's 1856 lens date and the 1878 and 1888 dates rest on LighthouseFriends. Owners of the converted dwelling are not named. Roster lines are the archive's own, unchanged. No Coast Guard entries apply here.
